text: Somewhere in your building, there is a student who slept in a shelter, a motel, a car, or on a relative's couch last night. Federal law gives that student specific rights. And every one of us has a part in protecting them.

The McKinney-Vento Act is a federal law. It keeps children and youth who lose their housing enrolled in school, attending, and on track to succeed. In Maryland, the State Department of Education oversees it. Here in Baltimore, City Schools' McKinney-Vento Program carries it out.

A brief history. In nineteen eighty-seven, President Reagan signed the Stewart B. McKinney Homeless Assistance Act, the first major federal response to homelessness. It created the Education for Homeless Children and Youth program. In two thousand, the law was renamed McKinney-Vento, honoring Minnesota Congressman Bruce Vento. In two thousand one, No Child Left Behind required a homeless liaison in every school district, immediate enrollment, and transportation to the school of origin. And in twenty fifteen, the Every Student Succeeds Act strengthened these protections, including support for preschoolers, unaccompanied youth, and college and career readiness.

In the twenty twenty-three to twenty-four school year, Maryland schools identified more than twenty thousand students experiencing homelessness. Fifty-seven hundred of them were here in Baltimore City. That is more than one in four of all identified students in the state, and roughly one in thirteen City Schools students. And our count has nearly doubled in five years.

Homelessness doesn't always look the way we expect. Most identified students are doubled up, staying with friends or relatives because they lost their housing. Others live in motels, shelters, cars, or places not meant for people to live. Young people living on their own, without a parent or guardian, are covered too.

Students experiencing homelessness must be enrolled immediately, even without records, proof of address, or immunization papers. They can stay in their school of origin when that is in their best interest, with transportation provided. They are automatically eligible for free meals, and have full access to every program and activity. If there is a disagreement, the student is enrolled while it is resolved.
Through its McKinney-Vento Program, City Schools helps families with uniforms and clothing, school supplies, transportation, laundry support, fee waivers, and connections to community resources.

Your part comes down to three words. Notice, refer, protect. Notice the signs. Refer the student to your school's McKinney-Vento liaison. Protect the student's privacy, because housing status is confidential. And never let missing paperwork become a barrier.

Stability starts at school. If you think a student may be experiencing homelessness, reach out to your school liaison, or call City Schools' McKinney-Vento liaison at four four three, six four two, two four two four.
